questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman's new book?
questions.stemZh: 关于这位女士的新书我们了解到什么?
questions.answerText: It has given rise to much controversy.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: With me today is Meghan Brown, an environmental activist whose controversial new book Beyond Recycling is making headlines. 今天和我在一起的是梅根·布朗，一位环保活动家，她那本充满争议的新书《超越回收》正成 为头条。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 开场介绍即定性句。主持人开场介绍嘉宾时用 controversial new book 直接给书定了性， 开场点题句往往就是答案句，不必等转折。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: controversial new book ↔It has given rise to much controversy. 形容词转名词化

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 与原文相反 It has been very favorably received. 说广受好评，与原文 controversial(有争议)方向相 反；有争议恰恰意味着评价两极，不等于一致叫好。 借用原文：controversial new book C) 原词陷阱 It was primarily written for vegetarians. 借了后文反复出现的素食话题，但录音从未说这 本书「主要写给素食者」；vegetarian 是真听到的词，可这句话原文没说，是典型听到原词 就想选。 借用原文：They know I'm a vegetarian D) 原词陷阱 It offends many environmentalists. 用了 environmentalist 这个反复出现的词，但原文 说她被人「描绘成」环保活动家，从没说这本书「冒犯了许多环保人士」，属凭原词臆造。 借用原文：as a radical animal rights activist and environmentalist

options.label: A
options.text: It has given rise to much controversy.
options.textZh: 它引起了很多争议。

options.label: B
options.text: It has been very favorably received.
options.textZh: 它受到了非常好的评价。

options.label: C

options.textZh: 它主要是为素食者写的。

options.label: D

questions.stem: What do some critics say about the author of the book?
questions.stemZh: 一些批评者对这本书的作者有何评价?
questions.answerText: She tries to force people to accept her radical ideas.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Critics of your book assert that you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country. Some claim that you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet and make private transport illegal. 你这本书的批评者断言，你想把激进的改变强加给整个国家。有人声称你想强迫所有人吃素 食、把私人交通工具变成非法。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: Critics assert 转述信号。出现 Critics of your book assert that 这一转述信号，明确告诉 你下面就是批评者的说法，正对题干的 critics，是答案句标志。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country ↔ She tries to force people to accept her radical ideas. 几近同词的核心保留

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 She neglects people's efforts in animal protection. 提到 animal protection 蹭了动物话 题，但批评者从没说她「忽视他人的动保努力」，原文无此评价。 C) 原词陷阱 She ignores the various benefits of public transport. 用了反复出现的 public transport，但批评者根本没说她「无视公共交通的好处」——恰恰相反，她是支持公共交 通的，这是把话题词乱拼成的指控。 借用原文：make private transport illegal D) 张冠李戴 She insists vegetarians are harming the environment. 用了 vegetarian 和 environment 两个高频词，但批评者说的是她想强迫大家吃素，绝非说「素食者在破坏环 境」，意思被拧反了。 借用原文：you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet

options.label: A
options.text: She neglects people's efforts in animal protection.
options.textZh: 她忽视了人们在动物保护方面的努力。

options.label: B
options.text: She tries to force people to accept her radical ideas.
options.textZh: 她试图强迫人们接受她的激进观点。

options.label: C

options.textZh: 她忽视了公共交通的各种好处。

options.label: D

options.textZh: 她坚持认为素食者正在危害环境。

questions.stem: What does the woman claim about the diet changes she suggested?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士对她建议的饮食改变有何主张?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: In my guidelines for saving the environment, I suggest modest changes, like eating vegetarian meals two days a week. 在我那份保护环境的指南里，我建议的是温和的改变，比如每周吃两天素食。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: I suggest+定性词。她亲口说 I suggest modest changes，suggest 后紧跟的形容词就是 她对所建议改变的定性，是这题答案信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I suggest modest changes ↔They are modest. 同词直接还原

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 They are significant. 说重大，与她自述的 modest(温和)程度相反；她特意强调改变不 大，significant 正好拧反。 借用原文：I suggest modest changes B) 张冠李戴 They are revolutionary. 革命性，呼应了前文批评者说的 radical，但那是批评者的指控， 她本人恰恰否认并改称 modest，把批评口吻当成她的定性就上当了。 借用原文：force radical changes C) 未提及 They are rational. 理性的，听起来像褒义合理，但录音里她用的词是 modest 而非 rational，原文从未称这些改变「理性」。

options.label: A
options.textZh: 它们是重大的。

options.label: B
options.textZh: 它们是革命性的。

options.label: C
options.textZh: 它们是合理的。

options.label: D
options.textZh: 它们是适度的。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about her suggested tax increase?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士对她建议的增税有何看法?
questions.answerText: It would help to protect the environment.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: But the taxes I suggest aren't that high, less than 3% only. Plus, the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection, which benefits everyone. 但我建议的税率没那么高，只有不到3%。而且，所产生的钱会被用于环境保护，这对每个 人都有益。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: Plus 之后补出关键好处。她先用 But 澄清税不高，再用 Plus, the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection 补出加税的去向与好处，Plus 引出的 这句才是她想强调的作用，是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection ↔ It would help to protect the environment. 措施钱去向=保护环境

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 It would generate money for public health. 借了原文 the money generated，但钱的 去向是 environmental protection(环保)而非 public health(公共卫生)，把用途偷换了。 借用原文：the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection C) 未提及 It would need support from the general public. 听着合理，但她谈加税时只说税率低、 钱用于环保，从没说这措施「需要公众支持」，是无中生有。 D) 张冠李戴 It would force poor people to change their diet. 含 force 和 poor people，但这是主持 人质疑时的说法(第9段)，正是她要反驳的，不是她自己对加税的说法，题干问的是她怎么 说。 借用原文：Those taxes could force poor people to adopt your life choices. 1 M: With me in the studio today is Ms. Jane Logan, author of a new book, Secrets to Success. She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success. So Ms. Logan, in your book, you claim that successful people have many things in common. For instance, they know their strengths when pursuing a goal. M: 今天和我一起在演播室的是 Jane Logan 女士，她是新书《成功的秘密》的作者。她声称已经揭示了 人们如何取得成功。那么 Logan 女士，在您的书中，您说成功人士有许多共同点。比如，他们在追求目 标时了解自己的优势。 2 W: That's right. They also tend to be motivated by a negative or positive life event. They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them. W: 没错。他们也往往会被生活中的负面或正面事件所激励。他们把自己的成功归功于生命中有相信他们 的人。 3 M: You also write that there are a number of different factors related to success. And while successful people are driven to achieve their goals, the ultra successful have even greater ambition. M: 您还写道，有许多不同的因素与成功相关。虽然成功人士都有动力去实现目标，但超级成功人士有着 更大的抱负。 4 W: Yes, greater ambition as well as a burning desire to be the best of the best is also a common characteristic. W: 是的,更大的抱负以及成为佼佼者的强烈渴望也是一个共同特征。 5 M: Right. So those who are determined don't see obstacles as something that prevents success, but mere inconveniences that need to be overcome. M: 对。所以那些意志坚定的人不会把障碍看作阻止成功的东西,而只是需要克服的小麻烦。 Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 6 W: Absolutely. Successful people are also optimistic as it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles that can deter us from achieving our goals. W: 完全正确。成功人士也很乐观,因为在意识到可能阻碍我们实现目标的障碍的同时保持积极态度很 重要。 7 M: That's a good point. All too often, people give up at the first hurdle. Would you say then that most successful people make it all by themselves? M: 说得好。人们常常在第一个障碍前就放弃了。那您是说大多数成功人士都是靠自己成功的吗? 8 W: Not exactly. They are usually good at cooperating with people and understanding the needs of others. W: 不完全是。他们通常善于与人合作,理解他人的需求。 9 M: So people will be willing to help them, I guess. M: 所以人们会愿意帮助他们,我猜。 10 W: That's correct. And this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect, whether it's with a colleague, an assistant or even a receptionist. W: 没错。这往往会带来很大程度上的相互尊重,无论是与同事、助理甚至是前台接待员。 11 M: Most successful people I know are very passionate about their work. Would you say that passion is the single biggest key to success? M: 我认识的大多数成功人士都对自己的工作充满热情。您认为热情是成功的最大关键吗? 12 W: Not entirely. There's a prerequisite, that is, you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion. If that exists, success will follow. W: 不完全是。有个前提条件,那就是你必须在一个培养热情的环境中工作。如果这个条件存在,成功就会随 之而来。

questions.stem: What has the woman revealed in her book?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士在她的书中揭示了什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success. 她声称揭示了人们是如何获得成功的。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 开头点题句。主持人开场介绍时一句 She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success. 直接交代了全书主题，开头点题正是主旨题的核心定位信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: how people achieve success ↔What makes people successful. "如何获得成功"="什么造就成功"

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 录音确说成功者 they know their strengths when pursuing a goal，A 把 strengths 单拎 出来问 "strengths 从哪来"，但 "strengths 的来源" 录音根本没讲，且它只是众多特征之 一，不是全书主旨。 借用原文：they know their strengths when pursuing a goal B) 未提及 B 问 "为什么很多人拼命追求成功"（原因），但全篇谈的是成功者 "有哪些共同特征"，从未 讨论 "人为何要拼命求成功" 这个动机问题，属无中生有。 C) 张冠李戴 C 说 "她（作者）如何实现人生目标"，但录音里这位女士是在 "揭示别人成功的规律"，谈的 是 people / successful people，不是讲她自己的成功经历，主语张冠李戴。

options.label: A
options.text: Where successful people's strengths come from.
options.textZh: 成功人士的优势来自哪里。

options.label: B
options.text: Why many people fight so hard for success.
options.textZh: 为什么许多人如此努力地追求成功。

options.label: C
options.text: How she achieved her life's goal.
options.textZh: 她如何实现了自己的人生目标。

options.label: D
options.textZh: 是什么使人们成功。

questions.stem: What do successful people attribute their achievements to?
questions.stemZh: 成功人士将他们的成就归功于什么?
questions.answerText: Having someone who has confidence in them.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them. 他们把成功归功于生命中有一个相信他们的人。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 归因信号 credit...to。被问者（女士）的应答 They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them. 中 credit...to（归功于）正是归因信号，它 后面跟的就是答案点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: someone in their life who believes in them ↔Having someone who has confidence in them. believes in=has confidence in

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 B "有人随时愿帮他们" 与 A 仅差核心词。录音说的是 someone who believes in them （相信），不是 "愿意帮忙"。"愿帮忙" 是后文 people will be willing to help them 才提 到、且属另一道题的内容，搬到这里就答非所问。 借用原文：people will be willing to help them C) 偷换概念 C "对自身能力有坚定信念" 把主语换成了 "自己"，而录音明确是 someone...who believes in them——是 "别人相信他"，主语方向相反。 D) 未提及 D "对生活持现实态度" 在整段归因表述里完全没出现，录音只说归功于 "有人相信他们"， 与 "现实态度" 无关，属无中生有。

options.label: A
options.text: Having someone who has confidence in them.
options.textZh: 有一个对他们有信心的人。

options.label: B
options.text: Having someone who is ready to help them.
options.textZh: 有一个随时准备帮助他们的人。

options.label: C
options.text: Having a firm belief in their own ability.
options.textZh: 对自己的能力有坚定的信念。

options.label: D
options.text: Having a realistic attitude towards life.
options.textZh: 对生活有现实的态度。

questions.stem: What do successful people do when faced with difficulties?
questions.stemZh: 成功人士在面对困难时会做什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Successful people are also optimistic as it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles that can deter us from achieving our goals. 成功者也很乐观，因为在意识到那些会阻碍我们达成目标的障碍的同时，保持积极是很重 要的。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 困难词 obstacles 附近的描述。被问者说 it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles，obstacles（障碍）这一困难词附近，紧跟的 stay positive 正是成功 者面对困难的反应。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: stay positive ↔They stay positive. 原话直接对应 Successful people are also optimistic ↔stay positive optimistic 与 positive 同义

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 A "相应调整目标"，但录音第 5 段说成功者 don't see obstacles as something that prevents success, but mere inconveniences that need to be overcome——是 "克服障 碍" 而非 "改目标"，方向相反。 借用原文：mere inconveniences that need to be overcome B) 偷换概念 B "努力让自己显得乐观"，录音确说 optimistic、stay positive，但那是 "真的保持积极"， 不是 "appear（装作）乐观"，selflessly 加了一个 "装样子" 的意思，曲解原意。 借用原文：Successful people are also optimistic D) 偷换概念 D "remain calm（保持冷静）" 与 C "stay positive（保持积极）" 极易混，但录音说的是 positive / optimistic（积极乐观），从未说 calm（冷静），用近义词偷梁换柱。

options.label: A
options.textZh: 他们相应地调整自己的目标。

options.label: B
options.text: They try hard to appear optimistic.
options.textZh: 他们努力表现出乐观的样子。

options.label: C
options.textZh: 他们保持积极。

options.label: D
options.textZh: 他们保持冷静。

questions.stem: What is one prerequisite for passion at work according to the woman?
questions.stemZh: 根据这位女士的说法,工作中拥有热情的一个先决条件是什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: There's a prerequisite, that is, you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion. 有一个前提条件，那就是，你必须在一个能培育激情的环境里工作。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 明示信号 prerequisite + have to。被问者直接说 There's a prerequisite, that is, you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion.，prerequisite（前提）加 have to（必须）双重 "必需" 信号，答案点就在其后。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: an environment that nurtures passion ↔A nurturing environment. 动词短语压缩成名词短语

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 A "an understanding leadership"，前提句只讲 "培育激情的环境"，全程未提 "领导"； understanding 一词倒是在别处 understanding the needs of others 出现过、但那是讲 "理解他人需求" 的合作，与领导无关。 借用原文：understanding the needs of others C) 原词陷阱 C "同事间相互尊重"，mutual respect 确在录音 this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect 出现过，但那是讲合作 "带来" 的结果、且属第 6-7 题语境，不是 "激情的 前提"，搬来此处答非所问。 借用原文：this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect D) 张冠李戴 D "highly cooperative teammates"，录音确说成功者 good at cooperating with people，但那是讲成功者自身的合作能力，不是 "激情的前提"；把合作内容嫁接到前提题 上属张冠李戴。 借用原文：good at cooperating with people Section B 1 The saying "blind as a bat" simply isn't correct. The truth is that all 1100 bat species can see and often their vision is pretty good, although not as excellent as other night-hunting animals. "像蝙蝠一样瞎"这种说法根本不正确。事实上,所有1100种蝙蝠都能看见,而且它们的视力通常相当好,尽管 不如其他夜间狩猎动物那样出色。 2 There are two main groups of bats, which are believed to have evolved independently of each other, but both from a common ancestor. The first group, known as the mega bats, are mostly medium-sized or large bats who eat fruits, flowers, and sometimes small animals or fish. These species have distinctive visual centers and big eyes. They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey. For example, Flying Foxes not only see well during daylight, but can also distinguish colors. They actually rely on their daylight vision and cannot fly during the night with no moonlight. 蝙蝠主要有两大类群,人们认为它们是彼此独立进化的,但都源自一个共同的祖先。第一类群被称为大蝙蝠, 多数是中型或大型蝙蝠,以水果、花朵为食,有时也吃小动物或鱼。这些物种拥有独特的视觉中枢和大眼 睛。它们利用视觉和嗅觉来捕获猎物。例如,狐蝠不仅在白天视力良好,还能分辨颜色。它们实际上依赖日 间视觉,在没有月光的夜晚无法飞行。 3 The second group, called micro bats, are smaller in size and mostly eat insects. These species use echolocation to find their way and identify food. Scientists have proven that despite their poorly Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. developed small eyes, these bats still can see during the day. When we consider the nightly lifestyle of these bats, we will see they have to be sensitive to the changing light levels because this is how they sense when to start hunting. Moreover, vision is used by micro bats to travel over long distances, beyond the range of echolocation. 第二类群被称为小蝙蝠,体型较小,主要以昆虫为食。这些物种利用回声定位来辨别方向和识别食物。科学 家已经证明,尽管它们的小眼睛发育不良,这些蝙蝠在白天仍然能看见。当我们考虑这些蝙蝠的夜间生活方 式时,会发现它们必须对光线强度的变化保持敏感,因为这是它们感知何时开始狩猎的方式。此外,小蝙蝠利 用视觉进行超出回声定位范围的长距离移动。 4 So the truth is, there are no bats which are naturally blind. Some species use their sense of hearing more than their eyes as a matter of adaptation to a particular lifestyle, but their eyes are still functional. 所以事实是,没有天生失明的蝙蝠。有些物种更多地使用听觉而不是视觉,这是对特定生活方式的一种适应, 但它们的眼睛仍然是有功能的。

options.textZh: 善解人意的领导。

options.label: B
options.textZh: 培育性的环境。

options.label: C
options.textZh: 同事之间的相互尊重。

options.label: D
options.textZh: 高度合作的团队成员。

questions.stem: What do we learn about mega bats?
questions.stemZh: 关于大型蝙蝠我们了解到什么？
questions.answerText: They have big eyes and distinctive visual centers.

analysis.label: 定位

analysis.label: 信号

analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 录音说 mega bats 是 They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey.，靠视 觉和嗅觉捕食；A 把别处提到的 sense of hearing 安到 mega bats 头上，且 mega 用的根 本不是听觉。 借用原文：They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey. B) 原词陷阱 录音确实念到 eat fruits, flowers, and sometimes small animals or fish，B 盗用了 small animals and fish 这几个原词，但只截取了一部分（漏了 fruits, flowers）、把偶尔吃说成 主食，是以偏概全的原词陷阱。 借用原文：eat fruits, flowers, and sometimes small animals or fish D) 与原文相反 录音说两类蝙蝠 both from a common ancestor，是共同祖先；D 称 mega 的祖先与 micro 不同，正好与原文相反，是把同变成了不同。 借用原文：both from a common ancestor

questions.stem: Why do some species of bats use their sense of hearing more than their eyes?
questions.stemZh: 为什么某些种类的蝙蝠使用听觉多于使用眼睛？
questions.answerText: To adapt themselves to a particular lifestyle.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Some species use their sense of hearing more than their eyes as a matter of adaptation to a particular lifestyle, but their eyes are still functional. 有些物种更多地依赖听觉而非眼睛，这是对某种特定生活方式的一种适应，但它们的眼睛依 然是有功能的。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: as a matter of点出原因。末段用 as a matter of adaptation to a particular lifestyle 直接给出更依赖听觉的缘由，as a matter of 是显式的原因信号，这句就是 Why 题的答 案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: as a matter of adaptation to a particular lifestyle ↔To adapt themselves to a particular lifestyle 名词化改不定式

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 录音末段明确 there are no bats which are naturally blind、眼睛仍 functional；A 称要 弥补天生没视力，与原文 naturally blind 的否定恰好相反。 借用原文：there are no bats which are naturally blind C) 原词陷阱 long distances 出自第三段 vision is used by micro bats to travel over long distances，说的是视觉的用途；C 盗这个原词来回答更依赖听觉的原因，答非所问。 借用原文：vision is used by micro bats to travel over long distances D) 未提及 录音从未把更依赖听觉归因于应对天气，weather 一词全篇没出现；D 是凭空添加的原因， 属未提及。 1 A study has found that educational TV shows come with an added lesson that influences the child's behavior. Children who spend more time watching educational programs increase their emotional aggression toward other children. This shows that children can learn the educational lesson that was intended. However, they're also learning other things along the way. 一项研究发现，教育类电视节目附带了一个影响儿童行为的额外教训。花更多时间观看教育节目的儿童会 增加对其他儿童的情绪攻击行为。这表明儿童可以学到预期的教育内容。然而,他们也在这个过程中学到了 其他东西。 2 This unintended impact has to do with the portrayal of conflict in media and how preschool-age children comprehend that conflict. TV and movie producers often incorporate an element of bad behavior. This is to teach children a lesson at the end of the program. Educational shows have pro-education and pro-social goals. However, conflict between characters is often depicted with characters being unkind to each other or they may use emotionally aggressive tactics with each other. Preschool children really don't get the moral of the story. That's because it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together. You need pretty complicated cognitive skills and memory skills to be able to do that. These are still developing in young children. 这种非预期影响与媒体中冲突的呈现方式以及学龄前儿童如何理解这种冲突有关。电视和电影制作人经常 加入不良行为的元素,这是为了在节目结尾给儿童上一课。教育类节目具有促进教育和促进社交的目标。然 而,角色之间的冲突往往被描绘为角色之间彼此不友善,或者他们可能相互使用情绪攻击性策略。学龄前儿 童实际上并不理解故事的寓意,因为这需要他们理解节目的所有部分是如何结合在一起的。你需要相当复杂 的认知技能和记忆技能才能做到这一点,而这些能力在幼儿身上仍在发展中。 3 However, parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing. Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot. Parents can comment along the way and then explain the message at the end. They should explain how certain types of behavior were not appropriate. Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard. This will help children interpret and get the message and help them learn to watch the show for those messages. 然而,家长不应该完全限制儿童的观看。家长应该与孩子一起观看并帮助他们理解情节。家长可以在观看过 程中进行评论,然后在结尾解释信息。他们应该解释某些类型的行为是不恰当的。这将帮助儿童解读和理解 信息,并帮助他们学会从这些节目中获取这些信息。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about children watching educational programs?
questions.stemZh: 文章关于儿童观看教育节目说了什么？

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Children who spend more time watching educational programs increase their emotional aggression toward other children. 花更多时间看教育类节目的孩子，会增加他们对其他孩子的情绪攻击性。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 话题词定位 + 反预期的负面定性。录音开头说研究发现教育节目"comes with an added lesson that influences the child's behavior"，随即点出 increase their emotional aggression toward other children——这个"与直觉相反的负面结果"正是研究要讲的核 心，是答案句的信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: increase their emotional aggression toward other children ↔ become more emotionally aggressive 动宾结构改写为系表结构

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 录音确实反复说 educational、added lesson，They acquire knowledge not found in books. 顺势编出"学到书本外的知识"，但 learn the educational lesson that was intended 说的是"学到了节目本意要教的内容"，并非"书本里没有的知识"，属听到 lesson 就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：learn the educational lesson that was intended B) 未提及 They learn how to interact with their peers."学会与同伴相处"听起来很像教育节目的好 处，但录音通篇讲的是孩子对其他孩子"increase emotional aggression"，恰恰是相处变 差，从未说学会良性互动，属未提及。 D) 过度推断 They get much better prepared for school. 与录音 learn to watch the show for those messages 的方向无关，录音从没说看节目让孩子"更适应学校"；它借"教育"联想到"上 学"，是凭常识推过头的正向结论。

options.textZh: 他们获得了书本上找不到的知识。

options.label: B

questions.stem: Why can't preschool children get the moral conveyed in the TV programs?
questions.stemZh: 为什么学龄前儿童无法理解电视节目中传达的道德寓意？
questions.answerText: They lack the cognitive and memory skills.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: That's because it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together. You need pretty complicated cognitive skills and memory skills to be able to do that. These are still developing in young children. 那是因为这要求他们理解节目所有部分如何拼接在一起。要做到这点，你需要相当复杂的认 知能力和记忆能力。而这些能力在幼儿身上还在发育之中。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 因果信号 That's because 直接领出原因。录音先说 Preschool children really don't get the moral of the story，紧接 That's because it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together——That's because 是明确的因果信号，其后两句给 出真正原因：需要复杂的认知与记忆能力，而幼儿这些能力还在发育。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: You need pretty complicated cognitive skills and memory skills ↔ They lack the cognitive and memory skills. "需要却还在发育"="缺乏"的肯否定转换

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 录音里 emotional 多次出现（emotional aggression、emotionally aggressive tactics），They are far from emotionally prepared. 借这个 emotionally 编出"情绪上远 未准备好"，但录音解释孩子领会不了寓意，归因的是认知记忆能力，而非情绪准备，属听 到 emotionally 就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：they may use emotionally aggressive tactics with each other B) 未提及 They tend to be more attracted by images."更易被画面吸引"是关于幼儿看电视的常识印 象，但录音解释"领会不了寓意"时根本没提画面或图像，属未提及。 C) 原词陷阱 录音确有 the portrayal of conflict in media 与角色间冲突的描述，They can't follow the conflicts in the show. 借 conflict 编出"跟不上剧中冲突"；但录音说孩子缺的是把"all the parts fit together"整体串联的能力，不是单看不懂冲突这一点，属原词陷阱。 借用原文：it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together

questions.stem: What does the passage suggest parents do?
questions.stemZh: 文章建议家长做什么？
questions.answerText: Help their children understand the program's plot.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot. 父母反而应该和孩子一起看，并帮助他们理解剧情。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 建议信号 should + 转折 instead。录音先说 parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing（不该完全限制孩子观看），紧接 Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot——should 加 instead 的组合，正 是"否定旧做法、给出新建议"的强信号，instead 后才是真正建议。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: help them to understand the plot ↔Help their children understand the program's plot. 代词还原 + 几乎同义复述

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 录音 program/programs 多次出现，Choose appropriate programs for their children. 借此编出"为孩子挑合适的节目"，但录音的建议是陪看并帮孩子理解，从没说"挑选节目"， 属听到 programs 就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot C) 原词陷阱 Outline the program's plot for their children first. 借录音里的 plot 编出"先给孩子概述 情节"，但录音说的是"帮孩子理解情节（help them understand the plot）"，是陪着理 解，而非父母先单方面 outline，属原词陷阱加偷换概念。 借用原文：help them to understand the plot D) 与原文相反 Monitor their children's watching of TV programs."监督孩子看电视"听着像合理建议， 但录音明说 parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing——反对单纯管 控，主张陪看引导。D 取的恰是录音否定掉的方向，属与原文相反。 借用原文：parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing

questions.stem: What should parents do right after watching the TV program?
questions.stemZh: 家长在观看完电视节目后应该立即做什么？
questions.answerText: Explain its message to their children.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Parents can comment along the way and then explain the message at the end. 父母可以在观看过程中随时点评，然后在结尾时解释其寓意。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 时间对照 along the way 对 at the end。录音把父母的动作按时间分两段：comment along the way（看的过程中点评）与 explain the message at the end（在结尾解释寓 意）。题干问的是 right after（看完之后），对应的正是 at the end 这一时点的动作，时 间标志 at the end 是定位信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: explain the message at the end ↔Explain its message to their children. 时间状语换补语，动宾近乎照搬

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 未提及 Check if their children have enjoyed it."看孩子是否喜欢"是看完节目后家长常做的常识动 作，但录音讲看完后是"explain the message（解释寓意）"，从未提"问喜不喜欢"，属未 提及。 C) 偷换概念 Encourage their children to retell the story. 与录音相近的是"看完后做点什么"，但录音 的动作是父母"explain the message（解释寓意）"，是父母讲给孩子，不是"鼓励孩子复 述"，主语和动作都被偷换，属偷换概念。 借用原文：explain the message at the end D) 原词陷阱 录音结尾说父母要 explain how certain types of behavior were not appropriate（解释 某些行为为何不当），Ask their children to describe its characters. 借"行为/角色"的联 想编出"让孩子描述角色"，但录音是父母讲解行为是否得当，不是让孩子描述人物，属原词 陷阱。 借用原文：explain how certain types of behavior were not appropriate Section C 1 While it has long been a practice in Asian countries, many people in Western countries have yet to embrace the no-shoes-in-the-house rule. For many in those countries, wiping their shoes before going inside is regarded as sufficient. After all, they may think a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone. But I can give you several good reasons why people should remove their shoes before going inside their homes. 虽然在亚洲国家这早已是一种习惯，但西方国家的许多人尚未接受进屋脱鞋的规矩。对于这些国家的许多 人来说，进门前擦擦鞋就被认为足够了。毕竟，他们可能认为一点点灰尘不会伤害任何人。但我可以给你 几个充分的理由，说明为什么人们应该在进屋前脱掉鞋子。 2 Bacteria are everywhere. They collect on your shoes when you walk along sidewalks, public toilet floors and even office carpets. In one study conducted at an American university, researchers collected microscopic germs from footwear. They found that up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe. And it only takes a little bit of dirt to damage your timber floors. The more dirt you track in, the more it scratches and the more often you'd have to clean. The extra scrubbing will harm your floors over time. Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors, especially high heels or shoes with pointed or hard parts. These can dent and scratch your floor. And if you live in an Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. apartment building, removing your noisy shoes is the polite thing to do out of consideration for your downstairs neighbors. 细菌无处不在。当你走在人行道、公共厕所地板甚至办公室地毯上时,它们就会附着在你的鞋子上。在美国 一所大学进行的一项研究中，研究人员从鞋类上采集了微观细菌。他们发现，一只鞋的外部可以聚集多达 421,000个细菌单位。而且只需要一点点灰尘就能损坏你的木地板。你带进来的灰尘越多，地板就越容易 被刮花，你就得越频繁地清洁。额外的擦洗会随着时间的推移损害你的地板。鞋子还会在地板上留下痕迹 和划痕，尤其是高跟鞋或带有尖头或硬质部分的鞋子。这些会使你的地板产生凹痕和划痕。而且如果你住 在公寓楼里，脱掉你那吵闹的鞋子是出于对楼下邻居考虑的礼貌之举。 3 Walking around with bare feet is actually better for your feet. It strengthens the muscles in your feet. Though many people are accustomed to wearing shoes during all their waking hours, the more time you spend wearing shoes, the more likely you are to incur foot injuries as a result. 光脚走路实际上对你的双脚更好。它能增强你脚部的肌肉。尽管许多人习惯在醒着的所有时间里都穿着 鞋，但你穿鞋的时间越长，就越有可能因此导致足部损伤。 4 And if people aren't yet convinced by my arguments, I can give one final reason. The dust and toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality in your home. Toxic chemicals are everywhere in our lives: insect-killing chemicals used on public grass areas, cleaning chemicals on the floors of public areas. By kicking off your shoes before you enter the home, you are denying entry to these harmful chemicals. 如果人们还没有被我的论据说服，我可以给出最后一个理由。你通过鞋子带入家中的灰尘和有毒化学物质 会降低家中的空气质量。有毒化学物质在我们的生活中无处不在：公共草地上使用的杀虫化学物质、公共 区域地板上的清洁化学物质。通过在进门前脱掉鞋子，你就拒绝了这些有害化学物质进入家中。 5 Given the amount of time we spend in classrooms, and the number of shoes that pass through them every day, you may well understand me if I were to propose a no-shoes-in-the-classroom rule. 考虑到我们在教室里度过的时间，以及每天有多少鞋子经过教室，如果我提议实行教室内禁止穿鞋的规 定，你可能会理解我。

questions.stem: Why don't many Westerners take off shoes before entering a house?
questions.stemZh: 为什么许多西方人在进屋前不脱鞋?
questions.answerText: They believe a little dirt harms no one.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: For many in those countries, wiping their shoes before going inside is regarded as sufficient. After all, they may think a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone. 对那些国家的许多人来说，进门前把鞋蹭一蹭就算够了。毕竟，他们也许觉得一点脏东西伤 不了谁。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: After all 引出真实想法。答案落在 After all, they may think a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone. 这句，信号词是 After all——它引出 "人们之所以不脱鞋" 背后的真实想法，是这 道原因题的落点。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone ↔a little dirt harms no one 同义改写：hurt anyone = harm no one

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 They are afraid of injuring their feet. 盗用了原文 incur foot injuries 这个 "脚受伤" 的字 眼，但原文那句是说 "穿鞋越久越容易伤脚"，是赤脚有益的论据，根本不是 "西方人不脱鞋 的原因"，属听到 "伤脚" 就误选。 借用原文：the more likely you are to incur foot injuries B) They have never developed the habit. 听上去合理，但原文只说脱鞋 has long been a practice in Asian countries、西方人 have yet to embrace the no-shoes-in-the-house rule，是在陈述 "做不做" 的现状，从未把 "没养成习惯" 点为他们不脱鞋的原因，属原文未 明说的推断。 借用原文：many people in Western countries have yet to embrace the no-shoes-in-the-house rule D) They find it rather troublesome to do so. 在原文里找不到对应——说话人只说他们觉得 蹭蹭鞋 is regarded as sufficient（就够了），从没说他们 "嫌脱鞋麻烦"，这是凭生活常识 脑补出来的，属未提及。

questions.stem: What is the finding of one study by researchers at an American university?
questions.stemZh: 美国一所大学的研究人员进行的一项研究有什么发现?
questions.answerText: A large number of bacteria collected on a single shoe.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: In one study conducted at an American university, researchers collected microscopic germs from footwear. They found that up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe. 在美国一所大学开展的一项研究中，研究人员从鞋上采集了微观细菌。他们发现，一只鞋的 外侧最多可聚集多达 42.1 万个单位的细菌。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: They found 引出研究结论。信号是 In one study conducted at an American university 点出研究，紧接 They found that up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe 用 "They found" 抛出具体发现——一只鞋上多达 42.1 万单位细 菌，这就是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe ↔ A large number of bacteria collected on a single shoe 具体数字概括为 a large number

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) Different types of bacteria existed on public-toilet floors. 盗用原文 public toilet floors 这个原词，但那句 They collect on your shoes when you walk along sidewalks, public toilet floors and even office carpets 是泛说 "细菌哪里都有"，并非那项研究的发 现；且 "不同种类的细菌" 原文也没提，属张冠李戴加无中生有。 借用原文：public toilet floors B) There were more bacteria on sidewalks than in the home. 盗用 sidewalks 一词，但原 文只把人行道与公厕、办公室地毯并列说 "都会沾菌"，从没拿 "人行道" 和 "家中" 作 more…than 的比较，这个比较是凭空加上去的。 借用原文：when you walk along sidewalks, public toilet floors and even office carpets C) Office carpets collected more bacteria than elsewhere. 盗用原文 office carpets，但原 文只把办公室地毯当作 "也会沾菌" 的并列地点之一，还用 even 表示 "连地毯都沾"，绝没 有说它 "比别处收集得多"，属偷换为最高级/比较级。 借用原文：and even office carpets

options.text: Different types of bacteria existed on public-toilet floors.
options.textZh: 公共厕所地板上存在不同类型的细菌。

options.label: B
options.text: There were more bacteria on sidewalks than in the home.
options.textZh: 人行道上的细菌比家中的多。

options.label: C
options.text: Office carpets collected more bacteria than elsewhere.

options.text: A large number of bacteria collected on a single shoe.
options.textZh: 单只鞋子上收集了大量细菌。

questions.stem: What is the final reason the speaker gives for removing shoes before entering a house?
questions.stemZh: 说话者给出的进屋前脱鞋的最后一个理由是什么?
questions.answerText: The chemicals on shoes can deteriorate air quality.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: And if people aren't yet convinced by my arguments, I can give one final reason. The dust and toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality in your home. 如果有人还没被我的论据说服，我可以再给出最后一个理由。你通过鞋子带进家里的灰尘和 有毒化学物质，会让家中的空气质量变差。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: one final reason 标志收尾理由。信号是 I can give one final reason——"one final reason" 明确宣告这是最后一个理由，紧跟其后的 The dust and toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality in your home 即 答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality ↔ The chemicals on shoes can deteriorate air quality 几乎同义、deteriorate 原样保留

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) Shoes can upset family members with their noise. 盗用第 2 段 removing your noisy shoes is the polite thing to do 里的 "noisy/噪音" 概念，但原文那是说为楼下邻居着想， 针对的是 downstairs neighbors 而非 family members，且它出现在中间、不是 "最后一 个" 理由，属张冠李戴加位置错位。 借用原文：removing your noisy shoes is the polite thing to do out of consideration for your downstairs neighbors C) 未提及 The marks left by shoes are hard to erase. 盗用第 2 段 leave marks and scratches on floors 的 "marks"，但原文只说鞋会留下痕迹划痕、会损伤地板，从没说这些痕迹 "难以清 除"，"hard to erase" 是脑补；而且这属第 2 段的地板理由，不是最后理由。 借用原文：Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors D) Shoes can leave scratches on the floor. 几乎照搬第 2 段原词 leave marks and scratches on floors，内容原文确实说了，但它是中间列举的地板理由之一，不是题目要的 "one final reason"，属答非所问的原词陷阱。 借用原文：Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors, especially high heels 1 Emotions are an essential and inseparable part of our consciousness. They are part of a built-in mechanism, which allows us to cope with the ups and downs of our lives both physically and mentally. When we hide our emotions and our true feelings, we stop being genuine, spontaneous and authentic in our relationships. When we put on cultivated and polished faces in the company of others, we stop being true to ourselves. Socially, it may be a good tactic to hide our true emotions, but morally it is also a breach of faith and trust. Although humans are more advanced and intelligent, animals are more genuine Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard. and authentic in their behavior and responses than human beings. The more educated we are, the less transparent and reliable we become. We are drawn to our pets because pets do not lie. 情绪是我们意识中不可或缺的重要组成部分。它们是内置机制的一部分,使我们能够在身体和精神上应对生 活中的起起落落。当我们隐藏自己的情绪和真实感受时,我们在人际关系中就不再真诚、自然和真实。当我 们在他人面前戴上精心修饰的面具时,我们就不再忠于自己。从社交角度看,隐藏真实情绪可能是一种好策 略,但从道德角度看,这也是对信念和信任的背叛。尽管人类更先进、更聪明,但动物在行为和反应上比人 类更真实、更纯粹。我们受教育程度越高,就变得越不透明、越不可靠。我们被宠物吸引,是因为宠物不会 说谎。 2 One of the first steps in dealing with emotions such as anger or fear is to acknowledge them as normal and human. There is nothing sinful or immoral about being emotional, unless your emotions make you inhuman, insensitive and cruel to others. Feelings of guilt associated with emotions are more devastating and damaging than the experience of emotion itself. So when you deal with the problem of emotions, you should learn not only how to control them but also how to accept them and manage the guilt and anguish arising from them. 处理愤怒或恐惧等情绪的第一步之一是承认它们是正常的、人性的。情绪化本身并无罪恶或不道德可言,除 非你的情绪让你变得不人道、麻木不仁和对他人残酷。与情绪相关的内疚感比情绪体验本身更具毁灭性和 破坏性。因此,当你处理情绪问题时,不仅要学会如何控制它们,还要学会如何接受它们,并管理由此产生的内 疚和痛苦。 3 Our brains are made up of a primitive inner core and a more evolved and rational outer core. Most of the time, the rational part of the mind controls the information coming from the primitive core and makes its own decisions as to what to do and how to respond. However, during critical situations, especially when a threat is perceived, the outer core loses control and fails to regulate the impulses and instinctual responses coming from the primitive brain. As a result, we let disturbing thoughts and emotions arise in our consciousness and surrender to our primitive behavior. 我们的大脑由原始的内核和更进化、更理性的外核组成。大多数时候,大脑的理性部分控制着来自原始核心 的信息,并自主决定做什么和如何回应。然而,在危急情况下,尤其是当感知到威胁时,外核就会失去控制,无法 调节来自原始大脑的冲动和本能反应。结果,我们让令人不安的想法和情绪在意识中升起,并屈服于我们的 原始行为。 4 In times of emotional turmoil, remember that emotions arise because your senses are wired to the primitive part of your mind which is self-regulated, autonomous and spontaneous. Your rational mind does not always deal with the messages coming from it effectively. These messages are part of your survival mechanism and should not be stifled simply because emotions are unhealthy and betray your weaknesses. When emotions arise, instead of stifling them, pay attention to them and try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver. This way you make use of your emotions without losing your balance and inner stability. 在情绪动荡时期,请记住情绪之所以产生,是因为你的感官与大脑的原始部分相连,而这部分是自我调节、自 主和自发的。你的理性思维并不总能有效处理来自它的信息。这些信息是你生存机制的一部分,不应仅仅因 为情绪不健康且暴露了你的弱点就被压制。当情绪产生时,不要压制它们,而要关注它们,试着理解它们试图 传达的信息。这样你就能利用自己的情绪,而不会失去平衡和内在稳定。

questions.stem: What should we do first in dealing with emotions?
questions.stemZh: 在处理情绪时我们首先应该做什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: One of the first steps in dealing with emotions such as anger or fear is to acknowledge them as normal and human. 处理愤怒或恐惧这类情绪的第一步，是承认它们是正常的、属于人之常情的。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 首步标志 one of the first steps。One of the first steps in dealing with emotions 直接 对应题干的 do first，是明确的首步信号，其后的 to acknowledge them as normal and human 就是要做的第一步动作。

analysis.text: to acknowledge them as normal and human ↔Accept them as normal. acknowledge≈accept、保留 as normal

analysis.text: A) 答非所问 Assess their consequences. 中的"后果"虽与第二段 more devastating and damaging 的 语气沾边，但原文从未把"评估后果"列为第一步，是借语气制造的答非所问。 借用原文：more devastating and damaging than the experience of emotion itself B) 与原文相反 Guard against their harm. 主张"提防情绪的危害"，但本段恰恰说"有情绪没什么可耻"、要 接纳，立场相反，并非要防备情绪。 借用原文：acknowledge them as normal and human D) 未提及 Find out their causes. 说找出情绪的成因，录音里并未把"找原因"列为处理情绪的第一步， 属凭常识联想的无中生有。

questions.stemZh: 当情绪出现时,我们被建议做什么?
questions.answerText: Try to understand what messages they convey.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: When emotions arise, instead of stifling them, pay attention to them and try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver. 当情绪升起时，不要压抑它们，而要留意它们，并试着理解它们想要传达的信息。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 建议信号 instead of...pay attention to。情境词 When emotions arise 与题干完全对 应，紧跟的 instead of stifling them, pay attention to them and try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver 是明确建议句，instead of（而不是）排除了"压 抑"、点出真正主张。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver ↔ Try to understand what messages they convey. deliver=convey、句式微调

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 Pay attention to their possible consequences. 用了 pay attention to（原文确有 pay attention to them），却把宾语偷换成 consequences —— 原文要留意的是情绪本身/其 信息，不是后果。 借用原文：pay attention to them C) 未提及 Consider them from different perspectives. 说"从不同角度看待"，录音末段并无"多角 度"之说，属听起来不错但原文没有的无中生有。 D) 与原文相反 Make sure they are brought under control. 借了全文反复出现的 control，但末段恰恰主 张 instead of stifling them —— 不要压制、而要倾听，方向正相反。 借用原文：instead of stifling them 1 Good morning, class. My topic today is how to feed a hungry world. The world's population is expected to grow from 6.8 billion today to 9.1 billion by 2050. Meanwhile, the world's population more than doubled from 3 billion between 1961 and 2007. Simultaneously, food production has been constrained by a lack of scientific research. Still, the task of feeding the world's population in 2050 seems easily possible. 早上好,同学们。我今天的主题是如何养活一个饥饿的世界。预计世界人口将从今天的68亿增长到2050年 的91亿。与此同时,世界人口在1961年至2007年间从30亿增长了一倍多。同时,粮食生产因缺乏科学研究 而受到限制。尽管如此,在2050年养活世界人口的任务似乎完全可行。 2 What is needed is a second green revolution. This is an approach that is described as the sustainable growth of global agriculture. Such a revolution will require a wholesale shift of priorities in agricultural research. There is an urgent need for new crop varieties. They must offer higher yields but use less water, nitrogen-rich fertilizers or other inputs. These new crops must also be more resistant to drought, heat and pests. Equally crucial is lower-tech research into basics such as crop rotation and mixed farming of animals and plants on small farms. 需要的是第二次绿色革命。这是一种被描述为全球农业可持续增长的方法。这样的革命将需要农业研究优 先事项的全面转变。迫切需要新的作物品种。它们必须提供更高的产量,但使用更少的水、富氮肥料或其他 Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard. 投入。这些新作物还必须更能抵抗干旱、高温和害虫。同样重要的是对轮作以及小型农场动植物混合种养 等基础知识的低技术研究。 3 Developing nations could score substantial gains in productivity by making better use of modern technologies and practices. But that requires money. It is estimated that to meet the 2050 challenge, investment must double to 83 billion US dollars a year. Most of that money needs to go towards improving agricultural infrastructure. Everything from production to storage and processing must improve. However, research agendas need to be focused on the needs of the poorest and most resource-limited countries. It is there that most of the world's population lives and it is there the population growth over the next decades will be the greatest. 发展中国家可以通过更好地利用现代技术和实践在生产力方面取得实质性收益。但这需要资金。据估计,要 应对2050年的挑战,投资必须翻倍至每年830亿美元。这笔钱的大部分需要用于改善农业基础设施。从生 产到储存和加工的一切都必须改进。然而,研究议程需要集中在最贫困和资源最有限的国家的需求上。世界 上大多数人口生活在那里,未来几十年人口增长最大的也将是那里。 4 To their credit, the world's agricultural scientists are embracing such a broad view. In March, for example, they came together at the first Global Conference on Agricultural Research to begin working out how to change research agendas to help meet the needs of farmers in poorer nations. But these plans will not bear fruit unless they get considerably more support from policy-makers. 值得称赞的是,世界各地的农业科学家正在接受这样一种广阔的视野。例如,今年3月,他们在首届全球农业 研究大会上齐聚一堂,开始研究如何改变研究议程以帮助满足贫困国家农民的需求。但除非这些计划得到政 策制定者更多的支持,否则不会取得成果。 5 The growth in public agricultural-research spending peaked in the 1970s and has been shrinking ever since. The big exception is China, where spending has far surpassed other countries over the past decade. China seems set to transition to become the key supplier of relevant science and technology to poorer countries. But developed countries have a humanitarian responsibility too. Calls by scientists for large increases in the appropriation of funds for public spending on agricultural research are more than justified. 公共农业研究支出的增长在20世纪70年代达到顶峰,此后一直在萎缩。最大的例外是中国,在过去十年中,中 国的支出远远超过其他国家。中国似乎将转型成为向贫困国家提供相关科学技术的关键供应国。但发达国 家也负有人道主义责任。科学家呼吁大幅增加公共农业研究支出的拨款是完全合理的。

questions.stem: What did Neil Postman say about the rise of television?

analysis.label: 判型
analysis.text: 题干 What did Neil Postman say about the rise of television? 指向 Postman 关于电视 兴起的具体观点，属典型的「找人找观点」细节题。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: As Neil Postman noted in his 1985 book Amusing Ourselves to Death, the rise of television introduced not just a new medium but a new discourse: a gradual shift from a typographic(印 刷的) culture to a photographic one, which in turn meant a shift from rationality to emotions, exposition to entertainment. 正如尼尔·波兹曼在其 1985 年出版的《娱乐至死》一书中所指出的，电视的兴起带来的不仅 是一种新媒介，更是一种新话语：一种从印刷文化到图像文化的渐变，而这又意味着一种从 理性到情感、从论述到娱乐的转向。 46. What did Neil Postman say about the rise of television? A) It initiated a change from dominance of reason to supremacy of pleasure. B) It brought about a gradual shift from cinema going to home entertainment. C) It started a revolution in photographic technology. D) It marked a new age in the entertainment industry.

analysis.label: 选项
analysis.text: A) ✓ 正确 a shift from rationality to emotions, exposition to entertainment ↔ a change from dominance of reason to supremacy of pleasure 预判要求「从理性到娱乐/情感」，a change from dominance of reason to supremacy of pleasure 同时锁住起点 reason 与终点 pleasure，是定位句的标准同义 改写。 B) 偷换概念 cinema going to home entertainment 把话题从「理性 vs 娱乐」偷换成「看电影 vs 居家娱乐」，原文从未讨论 cinema going。 C) 偷换概念 a revolution in photographic technology 把原文 typographic(印刷的) culture to a photographic one 中 photographic（图像化的，与 typographic 印刷化相对）误读 为「摄影技术」。原文谈的是文化形态而非摄影术革命。 D) 以偏概全 a new age in the entertainment industry 把原文对「娱乐文化全面侵入理性」的批判 性论述，矮化为「娱乐产业新时代」这一中性的产业事件，既缩小了范围（仅产业）， 又抽走了「理性被取代」的核心立场。 根据文章,文本阅读的优势是什么? A) A recent analysis found that most research mischaracterizes the relationship between music and skills enhancement.
B) In 2004, a paper appeared in the journal Psychological Science, titled "Music Lessons Enhance IQ." The author, composer and psychologist Glenn Schellenberg had conducted an experiment with 144 children randomly assigned to four groups: one learned the keyboard for a year, one took singing lessons, one joined an acting class, and a control group had no extracurricular training. The IQ of the children in the two musical groups rose by an average of seven points in the course of a year; those in the other two groups gained an average of 4.3 points.
C) Schellenberg had long been skeptical of the science supporting claims that music education enhances children's abstract reasoning, math, or language skills. If children who play the piano are smarter, he says, it doesn't necessarily mean they are smarter because they play the piano. It could be that the youngsters who play the piano also happen to be more ambitious or better at focusing on a task. Correlation, after all, does not prove causation.
D) The 2004 paper was specifically designed to address those concerns. And as a passionate musician, Schellenberg was delighted when he turned up credible evidence that music has transfer effects on general intelligence. But nearly a decade later, in 2013, the Education Endowment Foundation funded a bigger study with more than 900 students. That study failed to confirm Schellenberg's findings, producing no evidence that music lessons improved math and literacy skills.
E) Schellenberg took that news in stride while continuing to cast a skeptical eye on the research in his field. Recently, he decided to formally investigate just how often his fellow researchers in psychology and neuroscience make what he believes are erroneous—or at least premature—causal connections between music and intelligence. His results, published in May, suggest that many of his peers do just that.
F) For his recent study, Schellenberg asked two research assistants to look for correlational studies on the effects of music education. They found a total of 114 papers published since 2000. To assess whether the authors claimed any causation, researchers then looked for telltale verbs in each paper's title and abstract, verbs like "enhance," "promote," "facilitate," and "strengthen." The papers were categorized as neuroscience if the study employed a brain imaging method like magnetic resonance, or if the study appeared in a journal that had "brain," "neuroscience," or a related term in its title. Otherwise the papers were categorized as psychology. Schellenberg didn't tell his assistants what exactly he was trying to prove.
G) After computing their assessments, Schellenberg concluded that the majority of the articles erroneously claimed that music training had a causal effect. The overselling, he also found, was more prevalent among neuroscience studies, three quarters of which mischaracterized a mere association between music training and skills enhancement as a cause-and-effect relationship. This may come as a surprise to some. Psychologists have been battling charges that they don't do "real" science for some time—in large part because many findings from classic experiments have proved unreproducible. Neuroscientists, on the other hand, armed with brain scans and EEGs(脑电图), have not been subject to the same degree of critique.
H) To argue for a cause-and-effect relationship, scientists must attempt to explain why and how a connection could occur. When it comes to transfer effects of music, scientists frequently point to brain plasticity—the fact that the brain changes according to how we use it. When a child learns to play the violin, for example, several studies have shown that the brain region responsible for the fine motor skills of the left hand's fingers is likely to grow. And many experiments have shown that musical training improves certain hearing capabilities, like filtering voices from background noise or distinguishing the difference between the consonants(辅音) 'b' and 'g'.
I) But Schellenberg remains highly critical of how the concept of plasticity has been applied in his field. "Plasticity has become an industry of its own," he wrote in his May paper. Practice does change the brain, he allows, but what is questionable is the assertion that these changes affect other brain regions, such as those responsible for spatial reasoning or math problems.
J) Neuropsychologist Lutz Jancke agrees. "Most of these studies don't allow for causal inferences," he said. For over two decades, Jancke has researched the effects of music lessons, and like Schellenberg, he believes that the only way to truly understand their effects is to run longitudinal studies. In such studies, researchers would need to follow groups of children with and without music lessons over a long period of time—even if the assignments are not completely random. Then they could compare outcomes for each group.
K) Some researchers are starting to do just that. The neuroscientist Peter Schneider from Heidelberg University in Germany, for example, has been following a group of children for ten years now. Some of them were handed musical instruments and given lessons through a school-based program in the Ruhr region of Germany called Jedem Kind ein Instrument, or "an instrument for every child," which was carried out with government funding. Among these children, Schneider has found that those who were enthusiastic about music and who practiced voluntarily showed improvements in hearing ability, as well as in more general competencies, such as the ability to concentrate.
L) To establish whether effects such as improved concentration are caused by music participation itself, and not by investing time in an extracurricular activity of any kind, Assal Habibi, a psychology professor at the University of Southern California, is conducting a five-year longitudinal study with children from low-income communities in Los Angeles. The youngsters fall into three groups: those who take after-school music, those who do after-school sports, and those with no structured after- school program at all. After two years, Habibi and her colleagues reported seeing structural changes in the brains of the musically trained children, both locally and in the pathways connecting different parts of the brain.
M) That may seem compelling, but Habibi's children were not selected randomly. Did the children who were drawn to music perhaps have something in them from the start that made them different but eluded the brain scanners? "As somebody who started taking piano lessons at the age of five and got up every morning at seven to practice, that experience changed me and made me part of who I am today," Schellenberg said. "The question is whether those kinds of experiences do so systematically across individuals and create exactly the same changes. And I think that is that huge leap of faith." N) Did he have a hidden talent that others didn't have? Or more endurance than his peers? Music researchers tend, like Schellenberg, to be musicians themselves, and as he noted in his recent paper, "the idea of positive cognitive and neural side effects from music training (and other pleasurable activities) is inherently appealing." He also admits that if he had children of his own, he would encourage them to take music lessons and go to university. "I would think that it makes them better people, more critical, just wiser in general," he said.

blocks.text: To establish whether effects such as improved concentration are caused by music participation itself, and not by investing time in an extracurricular activity of any kind, Assal Habibi, a psychology professor at the University of Southern California, is conducting a five-year longitudinal study with children from low-income communities in Los Angeles. The youngsters fall into three groups: those who take after-school music, those who do after-school sports, and those with no structured after- school program at all. After two years, Habibi and her colleagues reported seeing structural changes in the brains of the musically trained children, both locally and in the pathways connecting different parts of the brain.

blocks.text: That may seem compelling, but Habibi's children were not selected randomly. P1 The trend toward rationality and enlightenment was endangered long before the advent of the World Wide Web. As Neil Postman noted in his 1985 book Amusing Ourselves to Death, the rise of television introduced not just a new medium but a new discourse: a gradual shift from a typographic(印 刷的) culture to a photographic one, which in turn meant a shift from rationality to emotions, exposition to entertainment. In an image-centered and pleasure-driven world, Postman noted, there is no place for rational thinking, because you simply cannot think with images. It overturned all of those habits of mind, fundamentally changing our experience of the world, affecting the conduct of politics, religion, business, and culture. It reduced many aspects of modern life to entertainment, sensationalism, and commerce. "Americans don't talk to each other, we entertain each other," Postman wrote. They do not argue with propositions, they argue with good looks, celebrities and commercials."

P3 At first, the web seemed to push against this trend. When it emerged towards the end of the 1980s as a purely text-based medium, it was seen as a tool to pursue knowledge, not pleasure. Reason and thought were most valued in this garden—all derived from the project of the Enlightenment. Universities around the world were among the first to connect to this new medium, which hosted discussion groups, informative personal or group blogs, electronic magazines, and academic mailing lists and forums. It was an intellectual project, not about commerce or control, created in a scientific research center in Switzerland. And for more than a decade, the web created an alternative space that threatened television's grip on society.

P4 Social networks, though, have since colonized the web for television's values. From Facebook to Instagram, the medium refocuses our attention on videos and images, rewarding emotional appeals—'like' buttons—over rational ones. Instead of a quest for knowledge, it engages us in an endless zest(热情) for instant approval from an audience, for which we are constantly but unconsciously performing. (It's telling that, while Google began life as a PhD thesis, Facebook started as a tool to judge classmates, appearances.) It reduces our curiosity by showing us exactly what we already want and think, based on our profiles and preferences. The Enlightenment's motto(座右铭) of 'Dare to know' has become 'Dare not to care to know.'

P1 According to a recent study, a small but growing proportion of the workforce is affected to some degree by a sense of entitlement. Work is less about what they can contribute but more about what they can take. It can lead to workplace dysfunction and diminish their own job satisfaction. I'm not referring to employees who are legitimately dissatisfied with their employment conditions due to, say, being denied fair pay or flexible work practices. I'm talking about those who consistently believe they deserve special treatment and generous rewards. It's an expectation that exists irrespective of their abilities or levels of performance.

P2 As a result of that discrepancy between the privileges they feel they're owed and their inflated sense of self-worth, they don't work as hard for their employer. They prefer instead to slack off. It's a tendency which many scholars believe begins in childhood due to parents who overindulge their kids. This thereby leads them to expect the same kind of spoilt treatment throughout their adult lives. And yet Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage. despite how these employees feel, it's obviously important for their manager to nonetheless find out how to keep them motivated. And, by virtue of that heightened motivation, to perform well.

P3 The research team from several American universities surveyed more than 240 individuals. They sampled managers as well as team members. Employee entitlement was measured by statements such as "I honestly feel I'm just more deserving than others." The respondents had to rate the extent of their agreement. Employee engagement, meanwhile, was assessed with statements like "I really throw myself into my work." The findings revealed ethical leadership is precisely what alleviates the negative effects of employee entitlement. That's because rather than indulging employees or neglecting them, ethical leaders communicate very direct and clear expectations. They also hold employees accountable for their behaviors and are genuinely committed to doing the right thing. Additionally, these leaders are consistent in their standards. They're also less likely to deviate in how they treat employees.

P4 This means, when confronted by an entitled team member, an ethical leader is significantly disinclined to accommodate their demands. He or she will instead point out, constructively and tactfully, exactly how their inflated sense of deservingness is somewhat distorted. They'd then go further to explain the specific, and objective, criteria the employee must meet to receive their desired rewards. This shift away from unrealistic expectations is successful because entitled employees feel more confident that ethical leaders will deliver on their promises. This occurs because they're perceived to be fair and trustworthy.

P5 The researchers, however, exercise caution by warning no one single response is the perfect remedy. But there's no denying ethical leadership is at least a critical step in the right direction.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay related to the short passage given below. In your essay, you are to comment on the phenomenon described in the passage and suggest measures to address the issue. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. Nowadays star chasing is prevalent among many teenagers. They take pop stars as their idols, imitating their way of talking, following their style of dressing9 and seeking every chance to meet them in person at great expenses.
writing.model: The passage vividly presents a common scene: many teenagers today are obsessed with pop stars, copying how their idols talk and dress and spending heavily just to see them face to face. In my view, this phenomenon deserves a balanced judgement rather than blind praise or total denial. Admittedly, taking an admirable star as one's idol can be positively motivating, since a hard-working singer may inspire young people to pursue their own dreams. However, when admiration turns into blind worship, the harm outweighs the benefit. Chasing stars at great expense drains teenagers' limited money and time, distracts them from their studies, and may even distort their values. To address the issue, joint efforts are needed. Parents and schools should guide adolescents to build a rational view of idols, while the media ought to promote genuine role models instead of empty fame. For teenagers themselves, the key is to learn from a star's strengths without losing themselves. Only in this way can idol worship become a source of growth rather than regret.

sentences.text: 延安有纪念馆、藏物品、得美誉（主语策略：原句主语） 主语仍是 Yan'an，三个动作延安有9个革命纪念馆，珍藏着……大量重要物品，因此享有 "中 国革命博物馆城" 的美誉：「有」has、「珍藏」可降级为定语从句、「享有美誉」用 enjoy / earn the reputation。主干立为「Yan'an has nine memorial halls... and thus enjoys the reputation of...」。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「珍藏……物品」降级成定语从句 「珍藏着中共中央和老一辈革命家在延安时期留存下来的大量重要物品」用定语从句 which house a large number of important items left by the CPC Central Committee and older- generation revolutionaries during the Yan'an period 挂在 halls 后；「因此享有美誉」用 and thus enjoys the reputation of the City of Museums of the Chinese Revolution 收尾，体现 因果。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 主句回指基调用一般现在时 has / enjoys；从句中「留存下来的」是已完成的旧物，用过去分词 left 作定语，无需另起时态。 单复数 「9个纪念馆」复数 nine memorial halls；「大量重要物品」复数 important items；主语 Yan'an 第三人称单数，谓语 has / enjoys 带 -s。 因果连接 「因此」用 thus / therefore，本句用 and thus 衔接果句，显出前因后果，比直接平铺更连贯。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Yan'an has nine revolutionary memorial halls, which house a large number of important items left by the CPC Central Committee and older-generation revolutionaries during the Yan'an period, and thus enjoys the reputation of "the City of Museums of the Chinese Revolution". 英语六级 2021年12月·第2套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
